headline: New Stoplight at Oak and Pine Divides Community, Inspires Surprisingly Passionate Letters
summary: City council receives 47 letters regarding traffic signal installation, ranging from 'grateful' to 'betrayed.'
content:
The installation of a new traffic light at the intersection of Oak Avenue and Pine Street has sparked what city officials are calling "an unexpectedly robust public dialogue" about the nature of progress, change, and whether yellow lights are "long enough."

The stoplight, which began operation last Monday, replaced a four-way stop that had served the intersection since 1987. City traffic engineer Brenda Moss called the upgrade "a standard infrastructure improvement based on increased traffic volume."

Residents have called it many other things.

"This intersection had character," wrote longtime resident Harold Finch in a 2,300-word letter to the editor. "There was an understanding between drivers. A mutual respect. An unspoken covenant of automotive courtesy. Now we just stare at colored lights like trained seals."

Others have embraced the change. "I've lived on this corner for 12 years and watched people absolutely butcher the concept of 'taking turns,'" said resident Diana Kowalski. "Last week I saw the light turn red and three cars actually stopped. I wept."

The controversy has spawned two Facebook groups: "Restore the Oak-Pine Stop Sign" (127 members) and "The Light Stays" (89 members). A third group, "Oak-Pine Intersection Neutral Discussion Zone," has 4 members and no posts.

City council member Raymond Price expressed surprise at the intensity of public sentiment. "We put up a stoplight," he said. "I've received more correspondence about this than the proposed library renovation."

The light's yellow phase lasts 4.2 seconds, which traffic engineers confirm is within standard parameters. Letters continue to arrive.
author: Janet Reeves, Community Correspondent
